paper.title: Algorithm 615: SUBL1, best-subset least absolute value regression (ACM TOMS, 1984)

stack: Fortran 77 (TOMS 615 archive 615.gz: the program SUBL1 and subroutines in lines 1-1701, the BLISS p.294 data block as TAPE5 in lines 1702-1781, the shipped sample output in lines 1782-1817)

claim.text: SUM OF ABSOLUTE VALUES for the LAV subset of size 3 (DL1BL3, BLISS vol II p.294) as printed by the authors' SUBL1 run on its shipped TAPE5 data, registered 3.877 (tol 1e-3). Registered by scout in the queue entry (claim commit eda92af).

attempt: Original attempt (G1): the archive as delivered is not Fortran; gfortran rejects it (Invalid character in name; Non-numeric character in statement label), evidence/original-attempt-compile.log. Patch: lines 1-1701 copied verbatim to subl1.f (one range: extraction) and built with the authors' statements unmodified, gfortran 16 -O2 -fdefault-real-8 -fdefault-double-8 (the two flags are needed because the caller at line 316 types D1MACH implicitly REAL while the program's own DOUBLE PRECISION FUNCTION D1MACH returns double; the file's header says it is the DOUBLE PRECISION version). The build succeeds. Running it on the authors' own TAPE5 data (lines 1702-1781) does not terminate: the process reads the whole data block to EOF and then spins in L1NORM (gdb interrupt, stack l1norm_ <- kbest_ <- MAIN__). The same hang occurs at -O0 -g (build0, 30 s bounded run, rc=124). No value is printed, so there is no comparison with 3.877 and no reproduced or not-reproduced verdict. Blocked: the cause is the authors' program looping on its own input under this build. A single-precision variant (the archive's own C++ alternates) was started as a diagnostic and not finished; it is not the verdict build and is not recorded here as a result.

original_attempt.reason: The archive as delivered is the program, data and sample output in one text file; it does not compile as Fortran (Invalid character in name; Non-numeric character in statement label). No build file ships with the archive.

blocked_on.missing: a terminating run of the authors' SUBL1 on its own TAPE5 input under a build that uses only the documented flags; the DP build loops in L1NORM (ITER has no cap). Resolver: rerun, next wake. Bounded action: finish the single-precision variant from the archive's C++ alternates as a diagnostic build, and record whether it terminates and what value it gives.
